description:
Chunky Money Ice Cream, this is one of those flavours that brought back memories of a younger person. My mum and I used to eat ice cream every Friday evening whilst watching a movie we hired from Blockbuster video. My mum was so disappointed when Chunky Monkey disappeared. 
I though it was about time we made it here (although I don't like banana ice cream!)

What you'll need:
500g Milk
300g Cream (heavy or whipping)
155g Sugar
20g Glucose
40g Skimmed Milk Powder
2 Egg Yolks for colour and texture (Free range organic or corn fed as they need to ORANGE)
4 Large Bananas (RIPE ideally) you can bake them at 150c (300f) for 10-15 minutes though to bring the sugars out and strengthen the banana flavour. 
50g Chopped Walnuts
50g Banana chocolate shapes )or whatever you can get/make)


The Skimmed milk powder i'm using at the moment is pretty poor and does not dissolve well, i'll need to change it. If you can't get glucose syrup, you can use glocose powder, dextrose or even corn syrup/golden syrup. The result will be basically the same.

Heat the base to 82c (175/180f) to cook the eggs if you're concerned.

Freeze for a few hours after loading up, then sit back, watch a movie and enjoy your Ben & Jerry's Chunky Money Ice Cream.

If you enjoyed this video, please consider liking and subscribing, plus pop over to our Instagram and Facebook pages linked below and say hello :)

Instagram: https://tinyurl.com/2p85zcxh
Facebook: http://tiny.cc/mmxosz
Website: https://www.polaricecreamery.com


Thanks and see you on the next video :)

comments.text:
It’s crazy isn’t it, the flavor of banana is isoamyl acetate which comes out during the steeping phase. 
As an interesting fact, it’s the first chemical compound used for artificial flavors that is also found in the actual fruit itself.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: ​ @PolarIceCreamery  Very interesting indeed. After doing a little additional reading, isoamyl acetate is apparently produced almost exclusively during the ripening process. Chat GPT suggests that 15 mins in an oven at 350F (which I did with fully ripened bananas) may denature the enzymes responsible for the metabolism of isoamyl acetate, but by doing so you may be acquiring additional caramelised notes, along with flavours produced from the maillard reaction.
comments.author: @doogyob

comments.text: After a terrible attempt at pistachio ice cream (even though my paste turned smooth, in the ice cream it turned gritty), I went back to this excellent recipe and used finely chopped pistachios instead of the bananas to steep. Then strained. The ice cream turned out absolutely incredible! And i got to reuse the pistachios in blondies. But needed to use way more milk in the first place because a lot of it stayed with the pistachios even after squeezing. I first steeped in the milk only, so ended up soaking the pistachios again in extra boiled milk because i had to add more. Anyway, it definitely turned out to be the best pistachio ice cream I'd ever had!
